natural_body: 40% SMB discount: +31% signups, +18% rev, -12% ret; judge at renewal

first.rationale: Current data shows onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Memory 31 and 86 both document durable gains from simplification and streamlining onboarding. Memory 91 supports activation lift. Rather than chase competitor pricing (which memory 73 shows erodes retention by 12% despite short-term signup gains), this experiment doubles down on what has reliably worked for our core SMB segment: reducing friction. Simplified onboarding is sustainable, doesn't commoditize our positioning, and addresses the immediate activation and completion declines. Referral incentives (memory 57) work well but only on established customers when activation is healthy. We need to restore baseline activation first. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) is valuable but requires a different capacity investment and doesn't address the SMB activation crisis. Verification of 31 and 86 will confirm the specific field-reduction and streamlining tactics that worked, allowing us to refine rather than reinvent. Standard experiment scale balances speed with measurement rigor.
